articles.title_en: Rivian’s Gambit for Full Autonomy
articles.summary_en: I’m sitting in a Rivian R1S SUV as it drives itself down the leafy streets of Palo Alto, Calif. , through areas crowded with touchstones of tech history. We cruise near the landmark HP Garage , the one-car workshop where Hewlett-Packard, and, arguably, Silicon Valley, was founded in 1939. I skirt Stanford University, where a team led by computer science professor Sebastian Thrun won a US $2 million DARPA Grand Challenge in 2005. The team’s Volkswagen SUV, named Stanley, became the world’s first vehicle to navigate a grueling 212-kilometer Mojave Desert course with no human intervention. This Rivian might look like any other electric SUV in this affluent town, with its concentration of tech bros, venture capital, and startups. But inside this boxy EV is something special: an Autonomy+ syste

articles.title_en: The Growing Proof That Autonomous Cars Save Lives
articles.summary_en: Plenty of people remain spooked by autonomous vehicles, or AVs. Some experts and policymakers have cautioned that AVs won’t necessarily make roads safer. When it comes to partial or full autonomy, the picture isn’t entirely clear, in part because there aren’t enough self-driving cars to make meaningful apples-to-apples comparisons. Yet mounting research suggests that self-driving cars crash significantly less often than people, and with far fewer injuries. Evidence also shows that advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and other building blocks of autonomy—some of which are already mandated on every new car—are also reducing occupant and pedestrian injuries and deaths, along with insurance claims. articles.summary_th: ผู้คนจำนวนมากยังคงหวาดกลัวกับรถยนต์ขับเคลื่อนอัตโนมัติหรือ AV ผู้เชี่ยวชาญและผู้กำหนดนโยบายบางคนเตือนว่า AV ไม่ได้ทำให้ถนนปลอดภัยขึ้นเสมอไป เมื่อพูดถึงความเป็นอิสระบางส่วนหรือทั้งหมด ภาพอาจไม่ชัดเจนนัก ส่วนหนึ่งเป็นเพราะไม่มีรถยนต์ที่ขับเคลื่อนด้วยตนเองไม่เพียงพอที่จะเปรียบเทียบระหว่างแอปเปิ้ลกับแอปเปิลได้อย่างมีความหมาย อย่างไรก็ตาม การวิจัยที่เพิ่มขึ้นชี้ให้เห็นว่ารถยนต์ที่ขับเคลื่อนด้วยตนเองชนกันน้อยกว่าผู้คนอย่างมาก และมีอาการบาดเจ็บน้อยกว่ามาก หลักฐานยังแสดงให้เห็นว่าระบบช่วยเหลือผู้ขับขี่ขั้นสูง (ADAS) และส่วนประกอบอื่นๆ ของระบบขับเคลื่อนอัตโนมัติ ซึ่งบางส่วนได้รับคำสั่งจากรถใหม่ทุกคัน ยังช่วยลดการบาดเจ็บและการเสียชีวิตของผู้โดยสารและคนเดินถนน รวมถึงการเคลมประกันอีกด้วย ที่หน้า ADAS สถาบันประกันภัยเพื่อความปลอดภัยบนทางหลวงพบว่าเกิดขึ้นโดยอัตโนมัติ

articles.title_en: Workshops Educate African Researchers On How to Publish With IEEE
articles.summary_en: Many researchers and students in Kenya, Rwanda, and Uganda struggle to access and publish scientific and technical articles because of financial barriers including publishing fees and subscriptions to research libraries. To help, IEEE has made its Xplore Digital Library more accessible by offering discounts on subscriptions and lowering fees to publish articles. But the number of papers published by technologists in the three nations still lags behind those from other developing countries. It might be that many researchers haven’t received training in methodology, been instructed on how to write academic articles, or fully understand the process for publishing in scientific journals. articles.title_en: Protecting Dynamic Industrial Robot Cable Carriers
articles.summary_en: This article is brought to you by Tsubaki KabelSchlepp . In modern automated manufacturing, six-axis articulated robots perform high-speed, multidirectional maneuvers under demanding operational cycles. However, as robot arms swivel, rotate, and extend, the electrical cables, fiber optics, and pneumatic hoses supplying them endure severe mechanical stress. Torsional twist, rapid acceleration, and repeated contact with machine structures often lead to premature conductor fatigue, insulation breakdown, and costly unplanned production halts. To overcome these multi-axis motion challenges, the Tsubaki KabelSchlepp Robotrax System provides a specialized three-dimensional cable carrier engineered specifically for complex robotic motion. articles.title_en: The iPhone Duo is actually a software story
articles.summary_en: Good morning, how did you sleep? Me, I had trouble until I started counting the number of times Apple used the word “AI” in its keynote (it was 41). In my dream, I was inundated with Elizabeth Holmes deepfakes and memes , which startled me awake. As I lay in bed, I calmed down by reading about how AI will “kill us all by the end of the decade, ” and then I got up and helped ChatGPT do my kids’ homework . Such a great day. As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe . more…
